question: Formation of slaked lime by the reaction of calcium oxide with water is an example of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**combination reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A combination reaction is a chemical change in which two or more substances react to form a single new substance.
 
• The reaction between calcium oxide (CaO) and water (H₂O) to form calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂) is an example of a combination reaction.
 
• This specific reaction is represented by the equation: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.
 
• Combination reactions are exothermic in nature, meaning they release heat during the reaction process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Displacement Reaction:**

 
 
• A displacement reaction occurs when an element reacts with a compound, displacing another element from it.
 
• For example, Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu.
 
 
 
• **Endothermic Reaction:**
 
 
• An endothermic reaction absorbs energy from its surroundings in the form of heat.
 
• An example is the reaction between barium hydroxide and ammonium thiocyanate.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition Reaction:**
 
 
• A decomposition reaction occurs when a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• For example, 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂.
 
 
 
• **Exothermic Reaction:**
 
 
• An exothermic reaction releases energy in the form of heat.
 
• An example is the combustion of methane: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat.
